blocks.text: SOP: welding and hydraulics in the shop

This is the working cut for RDW-SOP-2022-070 on December 15, 2022. Owen Pike asked for a written bound after the current path (Screens optional, fire watch tribal) stopped being honest. I am Jeilen Jones, Shop Helper, writing for Cal Dreher, Nina Soto, and Hank Morel. Primary host bay-04.ridgeway.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on tack a fitting while oil is still weeping, then open questions. If you are on the floor next shift, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the steps.

Screen up. Fire watch 30 minutes. Hydraulic lines capped. No weld on a wet fitting. I am not restating a hallway yes. tack a fitting while oil is still weeping is out because November 29 tack on a wet line smoked the bay. 18 minutes of fans. Owen will not do it again. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: watch=30, minutes=18, weeks=3, rags=1, smoke=1, cap=1, wet=1, screen=1. Sibling tickets RDW-2540 and RDW-SOP-2023-088. I will not reopen tack a fitting while oil is still weeping in a side thread because someone asked for a rate waiver. Nina Soto is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Hank Morel owns a leftover that is easy to skip: weld.ridgeway.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (39): refuse on tack a fitting while oil is still weeping, lock is screen, 30-minute watch, caps, no wet tack. I will not hide a process change inside a 'quick align' on RDW-2540.
If the screen is down and the next bay is full of rags, we are not welding.

What a skeptical lead would try first on bay-04.ridgeway.internal: the path Owen Pike actually has, not an empty-tote photo. Metric I will argue is a clean confirm, not a vanity units-per-hour. If we cannot show that path on shop.ridgeway.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Jeilen Jones will not accept a hallway yes as that proof.
